notes.title: Knight's End - The final game in the Skautfold series coming this Halloween.
notes.content:
The Finale has taken shape.

The last game in the Skautfold story-ark will be titled [b]Knight's End[/b], will feature Len the First Knight, and take place only days before the inevitable destruction of life on earth.

Gameplay will be a mix of exploration and a separate screen timeline based combat system, with active defensive and aggressive play using the final iteration of the Guard system.

Planned release date is [b]this Halloween, so October 31st.[/b]




If you wish to know more in detail read on.

[b]Story:[/b]
The finale will follow the First Knight Lennecia as she undertakes a personal journey to save Saragat from a rather unfortunate fate. To do this she will venture onto the now abandoned Waltham Industries factory site, and delve deep into its secrets, facing the worst possible adversary for such a mission, Waltham himself. 
The story takes place only days prior to the now broken Moon's pieces laying absolute and final destruction to all complex life on Earth, and just before the Human built Citadel is to take off from London with as many humans as it can carry for a possible escape.
The story wont revolve around some contrived way to save humanity from the pieces of the Moon, but rather her personal mission to save Saragat from a horrible fate that awaits him.

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
Exploration will be very similar to the original game Shrouded in Sanity, with easier navigation.
Expect a similar style an atmosphere as you delve into Waltham's deepest secrets on his factory grounds and below.
However Combat will take place on a different screen, akin to jrpgs where you are transported on contact with the enemy.
Combat uses a timeline based system where actions take time to execute and have different cooldowns, both for you and the enemy. At all times you can see exactly what the order is via the visible timeline, allowing for precise planning.
Unlike most turn based rpgs you CAN an should actively defend yourself, minimising downtime and rewarding good timing, using the correct defensive action, or taking a bigger risk attempting to parry.
Each of your attacks have a status effect tied to them, with 3 different types of qtes to increase damage and chance of applying the status tied to the weapon.
Good timing on defensive and offensive actions will reward you with Chain, a resource you can use to unleash one of three different finishers, all playing into the rock paper scissor style weakness system, where the old-school combat triangle comes into play.
The battlefield will be reactive in that all attacks will leave a mark, so by the end of some fights it will get quiet messy.

All in all combat may sound complex, but its far easier to understand in practice, and I worked hard to ensure its far more engaging than the old-school simple turn based combat systems of the past. Controls are fast simplified to ensure no slow and cumbersome menu browsing will occur.

Here is a sneakpeek at a test combat screen
[img]https://i.imgur.com/6zDHIE7.png[/img]

notes.title: 1.0 Release. Post launch plans outlined.
notes.content:
[b]The game is now officially out of Early Access.[/b]


However there will be further content updates in the coming days and weeks.

First of all more optional missions, more masks, additional modes, and like with both Shrouded in Sanity and Usurper, different playable characters down the line. Into the Fray was built to be a lot more scale-able than Usurper was so adding content is a lot more easy.


The game should be bug-free, all currently reported bugs were eliminated, in case of any bugs however please report them in as much detail as possible and I will fix them asap.


[u][b]I would like to thank everyone who brought the Early Access version and reported bugs, and/or provided feedback.[/b][/u]


Hope you'll enjoy the game.

Steve.

notes.title: Into the Fray release date set.
notes.content:
[b]December 5th.[/b]

[i]Into the Fray[/i] will be leaving Early Access on the 5th of December.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/893610/Skautfold_Into_the_Fray/

The game is a direct sequel to both [i]Shrouded in Sanity[/i] and [i]Usurper[/i], and features Hito the 3rd Knight as the protagonist.

The game will receive post launch support in the form of more modes and silly extras, but the release version will already feature a lot of extras. Like the obvious Steam stuff like Achievements and Trading cards.

Once out of EA development on the next game begins immediately, while ItF will receive periodic smaller additions to tie over. No DLC plans. If you are interested in the 4th game in the series you can always pop into our Discord and take a look and have your say, discord users had a lot of influence on me over the last game.

notes.title: Update #12
notes.content:
Changed:


-Drastic fundamental change as to how map flushing is handled, the issue is that GMS sometimes fails to operate at a basic level, this meant that when restarting a dungeon or leaving it sometimes the built in functions would not work. So some rooms would retain data and cause a massive bug possibly blocking completion until its restarted.

So I tried a different method and here we are, now upon restarting or leaving a dungeon the game will secretly restart ensuring ALL data is flushed, this took a while to implement but now its working and should prevent this bug from ever occurring again.

This might cause unknown bugs so please be on the lookout for data not saving etc.


Fixed:


-Asylum remained locked off in some cases. 

-Asylum lifts would not direct properly.

-Scene transition fade out was missing in some scenes.

-Morale gained warning appeared in inappropriate places, now fixed.

-Flamethrower full auto fire still had the parenting bug resulting in enemies going off to fight invisible things.

notes.title: Early Access timetable.
notes.content:
So the release of the early access version is getting close, I thought I take the time to lay out my plan for the duration for the early access.


First the early access version will only contain approximately 2/3rds of the story content, dungeons, and bosses. This was an intentional choice so I wont rush the late game content and allow me time to polish up the earlier segments before moving to the end.

My plan for the first week of early access is to polish up whats already present, while preparing the side content for the first 2/3rds of the game. This game will feature at least one or two optional dungeon per "turn" in the story, but optimally up to 3 optional areas per turn.

Once the initial polish is completed I will move on to optional features like visual customization, while I on a constant basis create new optional content.

When the first 2/3rds of the game is stable and close to finalized I will move to the endgame segment of the story and extra content. Early access should conclude with the release of the endings, while new game plus (planed to have drastic changes, like different weapons and enemies with more moves) will be added post full release similar to the previous two games.

I plan on having daily patches, with the exception of hot-fixes for serious bugs or issues, so far none of these have presented themselves but that usually changes when players get their hands on the game.

Thank you for reading and hope to see your feedback during early access and on our Discord server.
